notes.title: Bonuses and Limitations in building: Shape Your City, Strategically!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/a8caf46e0134c1fe8db7aff6563f0b877aff35b0.png[/img]
[h1]Permanent Bonuses from Functional Buildings[/h1]
We will introduce you to a gameplay element designed to elevate your city-building experience: the "Bonuses and Limitations in building" system! This feature encourages strategic planning and efficient module layouts, adding depth and exciting challenges to managing your grids.

Get ready to be rewarded for your architectural prowess! Functional buildings grant permanent bonuses to entire areas, encouraging skillful use of space and thoughtful planning. These bonuses are activated by functional buildings with a defined range and will affect all modules within that range.

[h3]What kind of effects can you expect? These bonuses can modify:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Module construction costs
[*] Maintenance costs
[*] Module operating efficiency
[*] Your final score
[/list]

To make this system intuitive, we've integrated clear visual cues on your 3D map. Grids under the influence of a bonus will be marked with an icon assigned to the functional building providing it.

[b][i]Grid without any bonuses[/i]

[/b][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/ef6d98a09da4d7444070e3f43bf4685b6ddc1db2.png[/img]

[b][i]Grid with one additional bonus from functional building[/i]

[/b][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/5aaabd9a7775447fa68f83e0c24b259ce4b5bfed.png[/img]

[b][i]Grid with two additional bonuses from functional buildings[/i]

[/b][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/348fb60be5cce8bfc3065858badf37ad7b8d269b.png[/img]

When you hover over a functional building or a grid, the game will conveniently show the building's range or indicate which building is providing the bonus. Even if the visual suggests a part of the grid is outside the range, the entire grid (all its fields) receives the same bonus. If a grid is influenced by multiple functional buildings, hovering over it will display the ranges of all impacting buildings. The same logic applies to the tactical map for consistent gameplay understanding.

[b][i]Functional building bonus area range[/i]

[/b][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/cc4e8b45cb80f736c4374e049d008698083ae15e.png[/img]

You'll also see all active permanent bonuses on your building panel, either as an icon that reveals information on hover or directly as information plus an icon.

[h1]Understanding Limitations: Pathways and Generators[/h1]
We're introducing two main limitations that will challenge your planning skills and ensure your modules are functioning optimally:
Building Pathways: Modules that require pathways simply won't work without them. Modules that are offline due to a missing pathway will be clearly marked with an icon.

[b][i]The modules lack a connecting path, as indicated by markers visible above them.
[/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/053bc617dbc42f1f60dc185177ef3bbf49ae9644.png[/img]

[h3]Generator Operation on Grids[/h3]
If a module needs power, it must be placed within the range of an appropriate generator. Each generator has a specific range, providing power to modules within that range. Modules may require a specific type of generator (small, medium, or large). Interestingly, if a module requires a small generator, higher types (medium, large) will also work, but smaller types, even in greater numbers, will not. Some modules, like pathways, don't require a generator at all.

[i][b]Small and medium generators range
[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/8bf6d3da55c7e6a7104cea4b0fdc60866a883ffe.png[/img]

[i][b]Large generator range[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/aca6a71d0ec3f3d2ad6905eba658a0e7a59501cf.png[/img]

To assist your building decisions, when placing a generator, you'll see a preview of its range. If a module requires a generator, the game will show the ranges of all generators that fulfill its energy needs. For example, if you're placing a 'Scene module' that requires a large generator, you'll only see the ranges of large generators. If you're placing a 'Standard Foodtruck module' that requires small generators, you'll see the ranges of all types of generators. The system will also inform you if there are non-functioning modules on a grid due to a lack of a generator in range. Importantly, any module "touching" a generator's range is considered within its range, even if most of the model is outside. Modules will remain offline until a generator is built within their range. The generator's range and any warnings about non-working modules will persist until you address the situation.

[i][b]Modules are not connected to pathway and generator
[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/83c5d5d80de0b8b51312e1c46457aacf5309d322.png[/img]

[b][i]Modules properly connected to generator and pathway
[/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/2190b49c2cabcc730ea2acd67429e2d6b701ab43.png[/img]
Perhaps some of you noticed that the same screen above showed two generators connected to these modules. As we can see, in this case, [b]just one generator was enough to fully power all visible modules[/b]. This simply demonstrates the capabilities offered by this functionality and the [b]potential for optimization and proper planning when building modules[/b].


We truly believe these new systems will add exciting strategic layers to your city-building endeavors. We can't wait to see the incredible zones that you'll create in the cities!

notes.title: How Fans 'Paint' the COPA CITY
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/b15abdf7d27d0189eb5db2b8f63923e44124900e.png[/img]
[h2]🏙️ How Cities Come Alive When Fans Arrive! 🌟 
[/h2]

Today, we will focus on the moment when crowds of fans begin to arrive to COPA CITY. This is an important moment when you will be able to observe the visual effects of your preparations for the football festival.

We are optimizing the visual representation of fans of individual teams in different districts. Our goal is to ensure that a given part of the city pulsates with the colors and spirit of a specific club.

Let's take a look at how it looks in the case of a previously neutral district that changes under the influence of arriving Flamengo fans:

[i]Fanzone and surroundings in neutral [b]COPA CITY[/b] colors[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/b4640fc731685592741c5cbaf01de4d69fef57a2.jpg[/img]

[i]Fanzone and surroundings in [b]Flamengo[/b] club colors[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/b67c953533b30b8a4c1e2bfa5cb2cfe850cc6af8.jpg[/img]

[h3]Noticeable changes include:
[/h3][list]
[*] The gate in the fanzone adopts club colors
[*] Ball-shaped balloons adopt club colors
[*] Cable car wagons and the cable car stations themselves adopt club colors
[*] [u]Not presented, but will also change colors - banners around the fanzone[/u]
[*] Signs on lampposts will adopt club colors
[/list]

As you can see, the visual signs of club presence will be numerous, and you will easily be able to recognize which district the fans of a given club are in. Additionally, your cities will be decorated with club banners, making the dominance of a specific team visible from a further camera perspective.

[i]Flamengo banners hanging on buildings[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/e464ced07dfaa491b79f018a74d4b521a117da60.jpg[/img]

We are constantly adjusting the number of elements so that there are not too many and do not cause unnecessary confusion, while still achieving the intended effect.

We are curious about your opinions on this visual aspect. Let us know! We would love to hear your ideas.

notes.title: What role do the most "faithful to the colours" play in Copa City?
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/ae3eb7de4bec1dfa02263ec44df2dddd8502b90b.png[/img]
Hi everyone!

You’ve surely noticed the announcement of another club joining Copa City – Borussia Dortmund. The fans of this club are known for their incredible displays and spectacular tifos, like this one:

[previewyoutube=7S2uL06WbAM;full][/previewyoutube]

Studying the reality of the club and the culture of football fans led us to the development of “club demographics” – which we mentioned in one of the previous posts. This led us to give a special role to ultras – as one of the key groups of fans in the game, having their own specific roles and functionalities.

This group of fans of a given club does not only have certain economic characteristics, which translate into needs that the player must meet in the game world by building structures. It also has active functions – for example, the player is able to order a so-called “Raid for the opposing club’s flag”, which in the short term may improve the statistics of a given district, but is risky – because in the event of an unsuccessful raid, it may significantly reduce security in a given district, and thus the player may lose control over the organization of the entire event.

This type of mechanism may cause an increase in tension between clubs in the city, which may result in the need to build additional police structures or solve specific decision quests. Making the wrong decision in these tasks may also be the reason for losing control over security, and thus excessive use of this mechanic may lead to failure.

We have introduced the ultras functionality to express how diverse and colorful the fan community is in Copa City. We hope that this type of action will be appreciated by the gaming community, and Copa City will become a more credible game thanks to them, which will provide players with a lot of joy and satisfaction.

To sum up - Ultras – strength, but also risk

Fans in Copa City are not only statistics and economy – now ultras appear in the game, who can dynamically influence the situation in the city. What does it mean?

🔥 “Raid for the flag” – you can order your ultras to take over the rival club’s flag. A successful raid improves the atmosphere and control over the district, but... if something goes wrong, the security level drops drastically. In an extreme case, you may even lose the opportunity to organize the event!

🚔 Tensions and consequences – rivalry between clubs can lead to increased tension in the city. Too frequent actions may force the construction of additional police structures or solving difficult decision quests. Wrong decision? Chaos in the streets, loss of security and the risk of defeat.

🎭 Multidimensional fan community – Copa City is not only stadiums and finances, but also the culture of football fans. We want every football fan to feel that the game world reflects real stadium emotions.

This is just the beginning!

We hope that you will like the new functionality and that together we will build an even more fascinating Copa City. Let us know what you think – will your ultras be loyal support or an uncontrolled element?

notes.title: Master the balance in Copa City - Devlog #3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/054c1430001ecd6d0fe9f401dd1abb3809a3bc15.png[/img]
[h2]Time and Space in Copa City – Always Limited[/h2]
One of the main elements creating the game’s atmosphere is its limited time in a single loop. Players race against a predefined deadline, just like in real life—a football match date that cannot be postponed. Regardless of the player's actions, the time available to organize all aspects is fixed in advance.

At the same time, depending on the map, the "space" available to meet fan needs by building essential infrastructure varies, leading to different approaches to planning the construction of individual facilities.

[previewyoutube=J3Cw1TjRy3M;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Fan Needs and Growing Numbers – The Challenge of Balancing All[/h2]
As we mentioned earlier, fan needs are a key aspect of balance and the central focus of the player. We categorized these needs into four groups:
[list]
[*] Safety
[*] Accommodation
[*] Entertainment
[*] Food
[/list]
Additionally, due to the demographic division of fans into three types, players will experience differences in need priorities—some fans will require better lodging, while others will demand more entertainment.

With the ever-growing influx of fans in the game, each club's needs are balanced in such a way as to represent a different structure and gameplay style. Players must adapt their strategies to achieve the desired outcomes.

[h2]Long- and Medium-Term Goals – Synchronization with the Football World[/h2]
The essence of Copa City, beyond organizing match day, is immersion in the organizational rituals and customs surrounding this event. We want the goals achieved by the player to directly correspond with the football world, ensuring that players feel they are playing a football-themed game at every level.

Setting medium-term goals for players also generates satisfaction over shorter intervals—after all, completing an entire match scenario takes several solid hours of gameplay, which poses challenges for maintaining motivation.

However, organizing a football match is a treasure trove of events, which we use in the game as "dynamic bonuses," or medium-term objectives. For example, having teams arrive at hotels designated and prepared by the player. Seeing club buses parked at assigned hotels will undoubtedly immerse players in the football festival atmosphere, as this is one of the iconic scenes at such events.

[h2]The First Whistle – The Main Objective in Copa City[/h2]
Of course, regardless of the above, the player's primary goal is to ensure the match can take place. To achieve this, a series of conditions must be met, including but not limited to:
[list]
[*] Proper stadium preparation levels for the match
[*] A specified number of fans in the city
[*] Meeting fan needs to a certain degree
[*] Completing specific points on the organizer's roadmap
[/list]
These elements combine to form the main goal—completing the game’s primary loop and starting the match on the stadium field.

[h2]Summary[/h2]
To summarize, building long-term player engagement in Copa City is key to achieving satisfaction in the gameplay. As mentioned above, we achieve this by rewarding players not only for the long-term goal of successfully organizing the city, stadium, and fans to allow the match and teams to take the field but also for smaller milestones like the arrival of team buses in the city or transporting teams to pre-match training sessions.

We believe this approach will give players the sense that organizing a match is not just about reaching the first whistle but a complex process that delivers satisfaction from managing various levels of challenges.

notes.title: Why is stadium neutrality so important to us in Copa City? Devlog #2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/e0781bd72f7150c06a499708280cf5b12047a1ef.png[/img]
[b][i]While preparing for the production of Copa City, we made several very important decisions regarding the basic design of the game. One of them is the maximum neutralization of the stadiums where matches take place in Copa City, which the player must prepare, as this is the core of the gameplay. In today’s article, I want to explain why we made this decision.[/i][/b]

Gameplay in Copa City revolves around two key elements – the city, including the stadiums, and licensed football clubs. The player's goal is to take on the role of event organizer and achieve the best possible results in the match organization process, measured by the satisfaction of the fans coming to the city and the revenue generated. This approach makes the player's role in relation to the clubs neutral in terms of main gameplay service – the goal is to satisfy the needs of both groups of fans, as well as to maintain a proper level of safety and balance between them, which is also one of the components of the player's success in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/cf62ded782811a0773b8efd5cd0d7d1ad9489213.jpg[/img]
To achieve an ideal balance between the clubs, we decided on an agnostic approach regarding cities. In this way, we simulate a match situation, drawing inspiration from events such as the National Cup Final, the Champions League Final, or the Europa League. This approach allows the player to fully focus on the organizational challenges behind match day without having to deal with the “home/away” aspect. In our opinion, introducing this element would disrupt the balance of the game at the level of the core economic principles in Copa City.

Of course, at the same time, nothing prevents the player from making such a decision in their own mind and choosing to focus exclusively on the needs of their favorite club, thereby disrupting this balance. Paradoxically, this approach means that Copa City can also be challenging in terms of maintaining safe balance, disrupted by such player behavior, who will be catering to the needs of their favorite club's fans.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/431a61de56dde1ca3847abc0357b864d4caabdd0.jpg[/img]
When choosing cities, and consequently stadiums, we also considered their topographical characteristics and the saturation of urban space with symbols associated with football. As a result, the game’s design will allow for map differentiation not only in terms of appearance but also in the style and nature of gameplay. This is one way to keep the player’s attention for a longer time.

Thank you for your support and for reading this post to the end!

notes.title: Olympiastadion Berlin announced as the next arena in Copa City
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/91f1c84b2b1fbcc6eb565f84a6cb00106bfa8663.png[/img]
Following the successful unveiling of the first football tycoon “Copa City” in June 2024, We are announcing the next city extension by [b]adding the Olympiastadion in Berlin to Copa City[/b]. This is another milestone on our path to launch the game in 2025, says [b]Jakub Szumielewicz (CEO and Founder at Triple Espresso)[/b].

“Copa City” was announced in June 2024 at the PC Gaming Show 2024. The game quickly made headlines in both sports and gaming media as one of the hottest independent productions announced this summer. Over 100,000 people have added it to their wishlists, and a community of more than 90,000 followers eagerly awaiting the title’s debut has formed on social media. The game will introduce a revolutionary twist to the tycoon genre, as the players will need to organize a top class football match and deal with ensuring safety and providing entertainment to the thousands of demanding football fans before the kick-off, utilizing diverse mechanics and strategic planning to achieve the “football fiesta”, a unique factor of satisfaction of supporters.

From the very beginning, when we announced 'Copa City,' we emphasized how important it is for us to collaborate with leading partners from the football industry, says [b]Szumielewicz[/b]. On day one we introduced [b]PGE Narodowy in Warsaw[/b] as the first arena in our project and promised that more stadiums would be announced soon. Today, we are proud to welcome[b] Olympiastadion Berlin[/b], one of the most incredible football stadiums in the world located in one of the most inspiring cities on our planet. Never before have players had a chance to host a football match in Berlin, manage the flow of football fans through its iconic streets and squares, and organize the final parade from [b]the Brandenburg Gate[/b] through [b]Tiergarten[/b] to the Olympiastadion.

[previewyoutube=ptZljv6o8oM;full][/previewyoutube]

Olympiastadion Berlin with the capacity of nearly 75,000 seats is the largest football stadium in Germany and one of the most important arenas in Europe. Since its full and successful renovation in 2004, the Olympiastadion Berlin has hosted top fixtures in global football: 2006 FIFA World Cup final, 2011 FIFA Women’s World Cup match, 2015 UEFA Champions League final and six games of the recent UEFA EURO 2024 including the final.

The announcement of the cooperation between “Copa City” and the Olympiastadion Berlin aligns with our previously revealed strategy of signing official licensing agreements with PGE Narodowy stadium in Warsaw, as well as with the top brands like Arsenal FC, FC Bayern Munich and CR Flamengo that will also be featured in the game. Upon its release in 2025, “Copa City” will offer players access to six world-class football clubs and three iconic stadiums.

notes.title: What Are Clubs in Copa City? Devlog #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/23857936b12681857b95ad4425966fdb8cd3d5f2.jpg[/img]
One of the most important elements in Copa City is football club fans. The gameplay revolves around them. To adapt this concept to a tycoon game, we had to create a unique approach—a matrix that allows us to present the fans of a given club in a way that highlights the significant differences between them.

[h2]Everything Starts with Needs[/h2]
Copa City is a tycoon game that revolves around the needs of the fans. Everything starts from there. When designing the system of needs, we divided them into four main areas:
• Need for food
• Need for accommodation
• Need for safety
• Need for entertainment (which we call the need for a football festival)

The expectations of the fans in the game are built around these four needs. The player's task is to adapt the city's infrastructure to meet these expectations. Importantly, each club will have a different way of realizing these needs—some will require better hotel facilities, while others will demand higher security levels at events—this will influence the player's strategy during gameplay.
Additionally, the needs of both clubs affect each other, meaning that each match-up will require a different approach to gameplay and strategy.

[h2]Demographics of the Fan Base – The Basis of Balance[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/4613ea89b77e081fa18037a447ef99db8daf1808.png[/img]
Another very important aspect of the game is the demographic structure of the fan base. To add depth to the game, we divided the fans coming to the city into three main categories:
• Fans
• Ultras
• Family supporters

Each of these groups focuses on different types of needs, as mentioned earlier, adding further depth to the gameplay. Depending on the club, the player must not only manage the "needs of the club" but also the needs of the various groups coming to the city.
For example, ultras will be a group of fans for whom identification with the club and the football festival atmosphere are the most important, while family supporters will prioritize providing attractions for children and ensuring a high level of safety in the city.

The demographic structure of each club is also different, adding another element that distinguishes clubs from each other. All differences between clubs are based on analyses of the behavior of fans of specific clubs, their preferences, and the priorities of different demographic groups. At Triple Espresso, we work with a scientist who holds a PhD in this field, specifically in the behavior of football fans 😊

Thanks to these aspects, choosing any club for a match will present a different organizational challenge, which is intended to make the gameplay unique in specific match-ups of particular clubs and cities.

[h2]Visual Component – A Sense of Completeness in Representing the Club in the Game[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053691/72228caaa59594742a6b99c5ffcc16ec38e6eba9.png[/img]
The visual representation of clubs in the game is a major challenge for us, so we approached it very thoroughly.
At Triple Espresso, in addition to our Art Director who ensures the visual consistency of the game, we also employ people who have worked on the visual representation of the biggest football club in Poland (from which country we originate). These individuals form a team that ensures all elements related to club branding and characteristic visual elements perfectly reflect the club and fan realities. We believe that club heraldry and symbols are among the most important values in the fan community—hence our very detailed approach to this topic.

Thank you for reading this text. We hope to see you in future articles where we will describe more elements of Copa City in detail. We warmly invite you to add the game to your wishlist!
